new_findings.title: the N6 guard pins only 3 of the 11 scene-hash column aliases and never checks the SQL call-site argument order
new_findings.trigger: a candidate contract renames one of the 8 unpinned column aliases, or the candidate migration permutes the 11 arguments of the lvw_scene_hash() call site
new_findings.expected: every one of the 11 hashed field names is bound to its DDL column, and the SQL call-site argument order is compared with scene_hash.fields
new_findings.actual: only time_base_num -> scene_revision.tb_num, time_base_den -> scene_revision.tb_den and revision -> scene_revision.version are pinned; the other 8 aliases are only checked for key presence, and the SQL call-site argument order is never compared with the field list at all
new_findings.reproduction: probe P01 (contract column_mapping.media_sha256 -> 'scene_revision.media_ref_id', fences re-frozen) and probe P02 (migration lvw_scene_hash(s.end_pts, s.start_pts, ...) instead of (s.start_pts, s.end_pts, ...), fences re-frozen): both runs exit 0 with 'RESULT: PASS' and a stdout byte identical to the unmodified control run (sha256 9ae799f05a732ddffb57c2049acef8ae071e9d132990d5b0c6c0aa3d08a2965b)
new_findings.impact: exactly the harm N6 named: a port that hashes a different column or a permuted argument order produces a silently incompatible scene hash and ETag, and the D0 machine gate reports PASS
new_findings.owner: ClaudeCode-D0-Implement (checker) - a code fix must go back to the implementer, not to the reviewer
new_findings.note: the current owner artefacts are correct (n6.sql_call_site_field_order_ok = true, all 11 aliases resolve); the defect is that the machine guard does not protect them

new_findings.title: the canonical Scene DTO on the new GET /api/v1/scenes/{id} is not machine guarded, so the M1 remedy can regress silently
new_findings.trigger: the overlay's new GET /api/v1/scenes/{id} 200 body is changed from the canonical Scene DTO to another candidate component (for example MultiShot_SceneRevisionInfo)
new_findings.expected: the new Scene GET 200 body must be #/components/schemas/Scene, because keeping the canonical Scene on /scenes/{id} is the whole M1 remedy (the design 1.1 review recorded it as evidence C02/C03)
new_findings.actual: the checker only verifies that every component the overlay references exists; it never pins the Scene DTO on the new GET. The overlay can therefore make /api/v1/scenes/{id} return a SceneRevision shaped payload - the exact canonical/candidate divergence the 1.0 audit called Fatal (F1/M1) - and still pass
new_findings.reproduction: probe P05 (overlay add_paths['/api/v1/scenes/{id}']['get'].responses['200'] body data ref -> #/components/schemas/MultiShot_SceneRevisionInfo, fences re-frozen): exit 0, 'RESULT: PASS', stdout byte identical to the control run
new_findings.impact: the design 1.1 remedy for the canonical Scene (M1) has no machine protection in the D0 packet; only a human reading the overlay would notice
new_findings.evidence: checks/probe-results.json (P05); checks/recompute-results.json n1.new_scene_get_body_ref (correct in the current overlay)

new_findings.title: malformed candidate input escapes as an uncaught traceback with an empty stdout instead of a deterministic finding
new_findings.location: check_overlay_merge line 1892 (metadata.items()) and line 1913 (add_headers.items()); check_canonical_compatibility line 1509 (jsonschema validator on the retained frames); check_contract_and_schema line 1200 (metaschema check)
new_findings.trigger: overlay.metadata_only or overlay.add_response_headers is a JSON list instead of an object; or the candidate schema carries a syntactically invalid regular expression in a 'pattern' (for example '([unclosed')
new_findings.expected: a deterministic E_* finding on stdout with exit 1, or a clean INPUT_ERROR with exit 2
new_findings.actual: uncaught AttributeError ('list' object has no attribute 'items') and re.error tracebacks on stderr, stdout empty, exit code 1
new_findings.reproduction: probe P22 (metadata_only = ['/api/v1/scenes']), probe P23 (add_response_headers = ['/api/v1/scenes/{id}']), probe P24 (ShotFrameRef.sha256.pattern = '([unclosed'): all three exit 1 with an empty stdout and a Python traceback
new_findings.impact: the exit code stays non-zero so the run is fail-closed on the exit code, but the tool's documented contract ('exit 1 = at least one deterministic check failed') is violated: an automated gate that reads stdout finds no finding at all, and the traceback can be misread as an environment failure instead of a rejected candidate. E_SCHEMA_META does not rescue the case: JSON Schema 'format': 'regex' is annotation-only, so check_schema() does not validate the pattern

new_findings.title: degraded validation is never disclosed: Report.note() entries are collected and dropped, and the run does not state which D0 pin it verified
new_findings.location: Report.note (533-534); report.note call sites 1040, 1204, 1496, 1500; main (2655-2696) prints only report.errors
new_findings.trigger: the optional jsonschema dependency is not importable, or the retained frame reference sample is absent, or the execution-control coordinate state is not WAIT_HUMAN
new_findings.expected: the run states which validations actually executed (metaschema check, retained-frame instance probe) and which D0 packet manifest pin it verified against
new_findings.actual: E_SCHEMA_META_SKIPPED, E_FRAME_REF_SAMPLE_SKIPPED and E_COORDINATE_NOTE are collected in Report.notes and never printed; the stdout of a degraded run is byte identical to a full run (sha256 9ae799f05a732ddffb57c2049acef8ae071e9d132990d5b0c6c0aa3d08a2965b in all three cases)
new_findings.reproduction: probe P25 (--frame-sample points at a nonexistent path) and probe P26 (a shadow jsonschema.py that raises ImportError is put first on PYTHONPATH): both exit 0 with a stdout byte identical to the positive control P00
new_findings.impact: the D0 gate evidence is exactly 'checker exit 0 plus the test log', and the tool offers no way to tell a full run from a degraded one; a future host without jsonschema would produce evidence that is indistinguishable from, and weaker than, this one
new_findings.note: honest note on the optional fallback: in THIS environment jsonschema 4.23.0 is importable (verified by the reviewer, recompute-results.json n4.probe_engine), so the candidate's own evidence did run the full metaschema check and the full retained-frame instance probe. No validation was omitted in the candidate run, and this finding is not a claim that a product gate was granted.

new_findings.title: the N5 entry serialization rule names one key order, says 'sorted keys', and the frozen example uses a third order
new_findings.location: canonical_domain_mapping.entry_serialization: 'Each nonempty language value produces one string: compact UTF-8 JSON object, sorted keys, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False. Keys kind, ref, lang, text. ...'
new_findings.trigger: an implementer follows the enumerated key order 'kind, ref, lang, text' instead of the 'sorted keys' instruction
new_findings.expected: one unambiguous key order in the machine contract
new_findings.actual: the same sentence says 'sorted keys' and then enumerates 'kind, ref, lang, text'; the frozen example uses the sorted order 'kind, lang, ref, text'. The checker defines FROZEN_DOMAIN_ENTRY_KEYS = ('kind','ref','lang','text') at line 431 and never references it, so the contradiction is never detected - only the example is
new_findings.reproduction: probe P03 (rewrite the example with the prose key order, fences re-frozen): exit 1 with E_DOMAIN_MAPPING, which proves the example - not the prose - is the authority
new_findings.impact: two legitimate readings of the machine contract produce different bytes and therefore different canonical Domains entries and different hashes; the example removes the ambiguity only for an implementer who freezes their own example

new_findings.title: the N5 example recomputation covers only the character domain and ignores the declared observation/inference routing
new_findings.trigger: a scene, action or unknown entry is serialized with the wrong kind or ref, or an item is routed to the wrong domain (observation vs inference)
new_findings.expected: the pinned rule is verified for every domain kind the contract declares (character, scene, action, unknown)
new_findings.actual: the recomputation hard-codes kind='character' and resolves only the character ref and source field; the example's own 'domain': 'observation' field is never read, and the scene/action/unknown refs and source fields are only compared as strings
new_findings.reproduction: reviewer recomputation of the scene/action/unknown entries from the same rule (checks/recompute-results.json n5.scene_example_derived / n5.action_example_derived / n5.unknown_example_derived) shows the rule is implementable, but no machine check would catch a divergence there
new_findings.impact: the N5 guard proves one worked example, not the rule it belongs to

new_findings.title: the implementation receipt's stated verify_pack result contradicts the log it hash-binds
new_findings.location: supplementary_read_only_verifications[0].result = 'passed 7408, failed 0' (line 148); the same prose in implementation-receipt-1.1.1.md line 71
new_findings.trigger: a reader takes the receipt's stated result at face value
new_findings.expected: the stated result matches the log the receipt binds by sha256
new_findings.actual: the receipt says 'passed 7408' while the bound log reports/v1-redesign/d0-worker/design111/logs/verify_pack.stdout.log (sha256 c0d2ebec64a86d1f2de344d347cc96ba4c3ee8c2e0bc7a569444ebcb6885e4e9, the digest the receipt itself lists) says 7475. The reviewer's independent run of verify_pack on the exact candidate tree reports 7476 / 0
new_findings.impact: immaterial to the D0 gate (verify_pack is not a stage-control command and the hash-bound log is present and correct), but the 7408 figure is stale (it is the 1.1 receipt's number) and the receipt is the artefact a reader trusts. The 7475 vs 7476 delta is explained by the MANIFEST.sha256 line count: 4818 of the 7476 checks are one per manifest line, so a one-line difference at run time accounts for it

new_findings.title: the D0 packet manifest pin is CLI-overridable and the run never records which pin it verified
new_findings.trigger: a run is executed with an overridden pin, or a reader wants to confirm which pin a PASS was produced under
new_findings.expected: the run records the pin it verified against
new_findings.actual: the default is the hardcoded owner digest 04d3bfb4... (independently confirmed by the reviewer to equal the owner supplied manifest digest), and the frozen D0 commands in stage-control.json carry no override, so the gate run uses the default. But the checker prints no pin, so a PASS produced under an overridden pin is indistinguishable from a default-pin PASS. The implementation's own synthetic suite has to override the pin (a synthetic tree can never satisfy the default), so the default pin is only exercised by the two tests that run against the real root
new_findings.impact: low for the current candidate (the pin value, the two stale-pin negatives and the packet inventory were all independently reproduced by the reviewer), but the evidence does not self-describe

not_assessed_here: No product gate, product acceptance, Stage PASS or human signature is assessed or implied. The product stays at R1 / WAIT_HUMAN; the 621b1bf experience signature is still absent; the samples stay NOT_MATERIALIZED_NOT_FROZEN.
This offline D0 packet is not product Gate 0.

The original 22 findings of the first D0-B review were resolved at design level by the design 1.1 authority and the prior independent design 1.1 review. This review re-verified the preserved obligations at the surfaces they changed (the canonical Scene alias, the canonical V2 batch body, the canonical FrameRef narrowing, the old R1 packet manifest, the canonical contract hashes, the frozen denominators, the sample allocation, the budget arithmetic) and did not relaunch the whole original design audit.

No model inference, GPU, media/FFmpeg, service, browser, network, install, provider switch, product database or push was performed. The only SQL executed was an in-memory SQLite run of the canonical contracts/storage.sql DDL performed by the existing tools/verify_pack.py in a temporary copy; the candidate migration SQL was parsed as text and never executed.
The provider/model identity of the implementer is self-reported and was NOT independently verified.
The retained-frame instance probe, the metaschema probe and the effective-openapi merge are design checks; no runtime header, no product response and no real sample were produced or observed.
